evidence.fitness: A vision researcher could build on the code (it is small, reproducible, fast) but the finding is the textbook expectation: Triggs et al. (2000) and Hartley & Zisserman ch. 18-19 treat intrinsics as BA unknowns; Fraser (1997, ISPRS J. Photogramm. 52:149) 'Digital camera self-calibration' established self-calibrating BA with radial terms in photogrammetry; Snavely, Seitz & Szeliski (2006, Photo Tourism / Bundler) initialise f from EXIF and solve f, k1, k2 per camera in BA, and COLMAP (Schonberger & Frahm 2016) refines focal and distortion by default. Nearest prior work is therefore Bundler/COLMAP practice, and the result (focal free removes a wrong-EXIF penalty; needs enough views and low noise) is sound but not new. What would be new - when the fixating orbit becomes critical, model mismatch (render k1,k2, fit k1), per-camera focal, real data with a known calibration - is listed under Next steps, not done. The repository's own programme sensing-selfcal (PROGRAMMES.md:118) is the natural home and is not linked.
evidence.domain: Method matches standard practice (Levenberg-Marquardt/TRF BA with shared intrinsics, Brown one-term radial on normalised coordinates, verified against OpenCV's model). Departures a photogrammetrist would flag: (a) no uncertainty - 6 seeds, means only, no SE, CI or comparison to the Cramer-Rao bound (which I computed: reported f_err sits at 1.2-1.6x of it); (b) the rig has every camera fixating the origin, a configuration the critical-motion literature (Sturm 1997 CVPR; Kahl, Triggs & Astrom 2000 IJCV; Bougnoux 1998 for two views) identifies as degenerate or near-degenerate for focal estimation, and it is not discussed, so the 4-view failure and the f-distance trade-off ('free poses absorb most of a wrong focal') are not explained by the theory that predicts them; (c) section D compares fixed vs f-and-k1-free with no k1-only arm, and the distortion range (k1 to -0.3, ~30 px at the corner) is not tied to any lens; (d) render law = fit law. A sign-off as a correct teaching experiment, not as a research result.

defects.what: No test covers k1 estimation (section D, half the headline): breaking the solver's r^2 to x^2 leaves all 6 tests green. Add a test: run_trial(focal_err=0, k1_true=-0.2, est_k1=True, seed=0, n_feat=150) asserts |k1_est + 0.2| < 0.02 and selfcal < fixed.

Nearest prior work uncited and novelty overstated: refining an EXIF-initialised focal and k1/k2 in BA is what Bundler (Snavely et al. 2006) and COLMAP (Schonberger & Frahm 2016) do by default, and Fraser (1997) established self-calibrating BA; README calls it 'a new question' and cites only Triggs 2000 and Brown 1966.

No uncertainty on any cell: 6 seeds, means only, no SE/CI and no Cramer-Rao comparison (auditor's CRLB puts reported f_err at 1.2-1.6x the bound), so small effects like the 1.1-1.2x gains cannot be judged.

Every camera fixates the origin, a near-critical configuration for focal estimation in the critical-motion literature (Sturm 1997; Kahl, Triggs & Astrom 2000; Bougnoux 1998); not discussed, so the f-distance trade and 4-view failure are left unexplained and may not transfer to forward or non-fixating motion.
Oracle is scored on a different triangulated subset (idx_t, from F_PX) than fixed/selfcal (idx, from f0), and 'true_pose' is computed and discarded.
Library inserts a sibling project's src on sys.path at import; pyproject.toml declares no dependency on sensing-ba/sensing-recon, so `pip install` of the package alone fails on import.
README says run.py takes about 2 min; it takes 46.6 s. README:28 '0.012 whatever the focal' spans 0.0116-0.0144.

verdict: A small, clean, fully reproducible synthetic experiment whose numbers are right: projection and triangulation match OpenCV to 1e-13, results.txt and the SVG regenerate byte-identically, the solver converges well inside its cap, and the recovered focal errors sit within 1.6x of a Cramer-Rao bound computed independently. Claims match the results file and the limits are honest. It misses the bar on verification (the k1-estimation path has no test; a seeded r^2 bug in the solver survives) and falls short as research: it confirms standard Bundler/COLMAP practice without citing it, reports no uncertainty, and does not engage the critical-motion theory that explains its own fixating-orbit results. Finished, correct, not new.
